item.title: [MLB.com] Rays-Brewers World Series Game 1 FAQ (Fri., 8 ET on FOX)
item.dc:creator: Adam Berry; Adam McCalvy

item.content:encoded:
They are among the five current franchises -- with the Mariners, Padres and Rockies -- which have never won the World Series. But that will change after a clash between the two teams that finished the regular season with the best record in each league. The Brewers won a franchise-record 103 games. The Rays won 98.
One of them will win four more.
“The World Series is about to be [between] two exceptional baseball teams,” Rays president of baseball operations Erik Neander said amid the sprays of champagne and pouring beer in the Tropicana Field clubhouse late Monday night. “It's going to be a blast to watch.”
When is the game and how can I watch it?
Game 1 is Friday at 8 p.m. ET and airs nationally on FOX and FOX Deportes with streaming on FOX One.
All series are available in the US on MLB.TV with authentication to a participating Pay TV provider. Games also are available live internationally, although not in Canada. Sportsnet is MLB's exclusive English language broadcaster in Canada for every postseason game, while TVA Sports will be covering the entire AL postseason and the World Series in French and Broadcaster RDS will cover the entire NL postseason in French.
Who are the starting pitchers?
What better way for the World Series to start than with Rasmussen facing the team that drafted him and dealt him to the Rays five years ago? The Rays obviously didn’t announce their rotation immediately after clinching a spot in the Fall Classic, but their ace will be on four days’ rest and ready to pitch Game 1 of the World Series, as he handled Game 1 of the ALDS and Game 1 of the ALCS. Tampa Bay has won 14 of Rasmussen’s last 15 starts, and the club should be able to roll out ALCS MVP Freddy Peralta -- another former Brewer -- on normal rest in Game 2 before turning to fully rested and ready options like Nick Martinez and Griffin Jax.
Misiorowski’s first pitch of NLDS Game 1 against the Padres was 104.8 mph, the fastest postseason pitch in the pitch-tracking era, which dates back to 2008. But it hasn’t been smooth sailing since then. The Padres made him work, fouling off an incredible 30 pitches in the first four innings to knock Misiorowski out of the game by the fifth at 88 pitches. Then the Dodgers battled him just as tough in Game 1 of the NLCS, seeing 94 Misiorowski pitches in 4 1/3 hard-fought innings in which he limited the damage to one run. Half of their swings -- 21 of 42 -- produced a foul ball.
“Miz, say what you want, you didn't see 105 [mph], whatever, but whenever he got in a jam, he got better,” manager Pat Murphy said that night after the Brewers won the game. “His innings are up to almost 190 this year. That's way over, way over what he's ever done. The kid's bound to be a little bit tired, you know what I mean? You can't expect him to understand what this is all about going this far and having to pitch this much this year with the pressure he's had on him.”
The good news is Misiorowski will be rested. Because the Brewers finished off the Dodgers in four games, he will have gone 11 full days off between pitching against an opponent in a different uniform.
What are the starting lineups?
Rays: Misiorowski isn’t exactly an easy matchup for anyone, but it would make sense for the Rays to use a relatively standard lineup leaning toward left-handed hitters against the Brewers’ flame-throwing ace.
Brewers: The lineup the Brewers used against right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto in Game 2 produced the second postseason game in franchise history in which five different players tallied multiple hits. Against right-hander Tyler Glasnow in NLCS Game 4, they came back from four runs down to finish a sweep. So, with the Rays likely to start Rasmussen in World Series Game 1, why not roll with the same batting order?
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
Rays: The Rays leaned heavily on their starters in the ALDS and ALCS, with Peralta, Jax and Ian Seymour making at least one appearance out of the bullpen. Seymour became a regular left-handed presence in relief, albeit with shaky results in ALCS Game 6. Closer Bryan Baker has finished each of the Rays’ seven postseason wins, working seven scoreless innings so far. Left-hander Cam Booser has clearly established himself as the top left-handed setup man in front of Baker, while Tyler Wells and Kevin Kelly will get the biggest outs against right-handed hitters.
Brewers: Brewers relievers are 7-1 with a 1.33 ERA (six earned runs in 40 2/3 innings this postseason, accounting for every decision in the eight team games so far. That comes after they led MLB with 48 wins and led the NL with a 3.40 ERA in the regular season. Their high-leverage arms are leading the way: Trevor Megill (5 2/3 innings), Aaron Ashby (12 1/3 innings; more on his historic showing here) and DL Hall (5 1/3 innings) have combined for 23 1/3 scoreless innings this postseason with a .096 opponents’ average, and Abner Uribe had not allowed an earned run while appearing in each of the first six team games this postseason until allowing two runs (and giving up the lead) in the Brewers’ come-from-behind 6-2 win over the Dodgers in NLCS Game 3. He didn’t pitch in Game 4, so he will be particularly well-rested.
Any injuries of note?
Brewers: The biggest question mark for the Brewers is right-hander Brandon Woodruff, who spent the past two weeks making a last-ditch effort to make the World Series roster. After throwing off the mound prior to the NLDS for the first time since abruptly scuttling plans for season-ending shoulder surgery in August, Woodruff threw 31 more pitches off a mound in the visitors’ bullpen at Dodger Stadium during a workout between NLCS Games 2 and 3.
“I’m not really holding back,” Woodruff said that day. “I’m going as hard as my body will let me right now, because that’s where we’re at. I’m doing it in what I think is a good and safe way. I wouldn’t get on a mound if I didn’t think I could get on a mound. … I wouldn’t go do what I’m doing if I didn’t feel like I could do it.”
Who is hot and who is not?
Rays: Caminero officially joined the postseason party in Game 6 of the ALCS by slugging a two-run homer off the left-field pole against Cleveland closer Cade Smith. Díaz hit .333 with four doubles, two homers, four RBIs and a 1.061 OPS in the ALCS, and he leads the league with six extra-base hits in the postseason. Palacios went 6-for-12 with a big two-run double in the ALCS, and Simpson once again established himself as the lineup’s speedy spark plug. Hicks, DeLuca, Walls and Mesa didn’t provide much at the plate in the ALCS, but their defense was invaluable.
Brewers: Bauers won NLCS MVP by driving in six runs (twice as many as any other player on either the Brewers or Dodgers in the series). His 12-pitch walk turned NLCS Game 2 in the Brewers’ favor, and his 11-pitch home run in NLCS Game 3 gave the Brewers the lead in the seventh inning. … Contreras is also having a great postseason, hitting .367 with five RBIs in eight games. … Chourio is hot and not, all at the same time. He has a team-best seven RBIs this postseason, but has hit just .171 (6-for-35). His leadoff home run off Blake Snell in Game 3 of the NLCS gave Chourio 18 career postseason RBIs, moving him past Andruw Jones for the most postseason RBIs before a player’s 23rd birthday.
Anything else fans might want to know?
• This will be the first World Series game at American Family Field, but not the first World Series game in Milwaukee. Both the 1957 Milwaukee Braves and 1982 Brewers played at County Stadium, which sat just to the west of where the Brewers play today. There’s a marker for County Stadium’s home plate on the concourse of the youth baseball and softball field on the site today.
• Teams to score first are 23-12 (.657) this postseason going into the World Series, but Milwaukee has bucked that trend this October, going 5-1 when conceding the first run. All other teams are a combined 7-22 going into Friday night.
• It’s been 44 years since the World Series came to Milwaukee, and that’s a big number in these parts. It was worn by Hank Aaron, the former Milwaukee Braves and Brewers star who hit his 755th and final Major League home run at County Stadium 50 years ago this year.
• The Rays are 92-0 this year, including the regular season and postseason, when leading after eight innings. The last team to go a full year, including the playoffs, with a perfect winning percentage and at least 92 wins in those situations was the 2002 A’s (93-0). The A's, however, fell in the Division Series to the Twins.

item.title: [wosu.org] Forget ‘woe is me’: Guardians playoff run, Cavs outlook gives fans reasons to cheer
item.dc:creator: Amanda Rabinowitz
item.description: The Guardians' improbable postseason run ended Monday with a 7-3 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series. Now, attention turns to the Cavaliers, who open their season Thursday on the road against Philadelphia. Like the Guardians, the Cavs reached the NBA's version of the final four last season, advancing to the Eastern Conference finals before their season ended. Ideastream Public Media sports commentator Terry Pluto reflected on the Guardians’ postseason
item.content:encoded:
The Guardians' improbable postseason run ended Monday with a 7-3 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series. Now, attention turns to the Cavaliers, who open their season Thursday on the road against Philadelphia.
Like the Guardians, the Cavs reached the NBA's version of the final four last season, advancing to the Eastern Conference finals before their season ended.
Ideastream Public Media sports commentator Terry Pluto reflected on the Guardians’ postseason run, including what might have been.
“They could have won this game or that game and maybe they could've found a way to get to the World Series,” Pluto said. “And they did some strange things with how they handled their pitching and a few other things like that. But in the end, they lost to Tampa Bay (who had) the best regular season record in the American League.”
Tampa Bay will face the Milwaukee Brewers in the World Series. Milwaukee finished with the best regular season record in the National League.
Despite the disappointing finish, Pluto said the Guardians have established themselves as a consistent winner.
“For me, the bottom line on the Guardians is I think they generally overachieved like they do most years," Pluto said. "They're relevant, they're fun to watch, sometimes frustrating, but fun because they go out there and they win more than they lose. They've made the playoffs each of the last three years. It's just kind of a smart, enjoyable organization, even if everything they do doesn't quite work out right.”
The Guardians also have a young core of players who could help keep the team competitive. Rookies such as outfielder Chase DeLauter, left-handed pitcher Parker Messick, outfielder Petey Halpin and infielder Travis Bazzana are among the players to watch. Their star third baseman, José Ramírez, is also under contract through the 2032 season.
Pluto said the team’s ability to develop talent and remain competitive is one of its strengths.
“You don't sit there and go, ‘Oh boy, all their stars are going to leave,'" Pluto said. "The front office ... with manager Stephen Vogt consistently find ways to put a winning team on the field, and they'll do it again next year."
With the Guardians’ season over, the Cavs, coming off a deep playoff run of their own, open the season Thursday night when they visit Philadelphia to face LeBron James and the 76ers.
Pluto said that run was significant because the Cavs had not reached the conference finals since James left Cleveland in 2018.
“The Cavs in some ways are mirroring the Guardians," Pluto said. "They're consistently making the playoffs the last several years. They have a star in Donovan Mitchell, much like José Ramírez. And Donovan has twice signed contracts to stay in Cleveland.”
Pluto said the Cavs, like the Guardians, could benefit from being overlooked by some analysts.
“It's interesting that a lot of the experts are sort of (saying), ‘Yeah, the Cavs are pretty good,’ and just kind of yawning about it," Pluto said. "I think that's a good position for the Cavs because I think the Cavs do better almost when they're ... under the radar or being ignored.
The Cavs made several changes in the offseason, including trading Max Strus and re-signing veteran guard James Harden. The team also added rookie Maleek Thomas and secured another young piece of their future, exercising their fourth-year team option on forward Jaylon Tyson. The move keeps the 23-year-old under contract through the 2027-28 season, with a salary of $5.6 million that year. Tyson had a breakout season last year, averaging 13 points per game and shooting nearly 45% from 3-point range.
Pluto said he believes the roster changes could help Cleveland take another step forward.
“They made a trade for a guy named Peyton Watson, a small forward that could help them," Pluto said. "Harden's an aging star, but I think he can help them more than the player he replaced, Darius Garland. I'm very upbeat on the Cavs. I think they're going to have a really good year."
Overall, Pluto said Cleveland fans have plenty to celebrate.
“We're fortunate right now, when you're talking about the basketball team was in the top four teams in the NBA last year and the baseball team just finished in the top 4, by the way, for the second time in three years, because they also were in the top four in 2024," Pluto said. "That's a pretty good run in Cleveland sports."
The Browns, meanwhile, are also 4-2.
“The woe-is-me, ‘I’m in Cleveland, my teams all stink’ — no, take that somewhere else right now," Pluto said.

Both pennant winners reached the World Series with timely hitting, sterling starting pitching, and managerial masterclasses, setting the stage for a historic series. item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers will meet in the 2026 Fall Classic on Friday, Oct. 23, with the winner claiming its first World Series title.
Both pennant winners reached the World Series with timely hitting, sterling starting pitching, and managerial masterclasses, setting the stage for a historic series.
Here’s a statistical breakdown, along with my favorite 2026 World Series predictions and MLB picks for the Rays-Brewers matchup.
2026 MLB World Series betting preview: Rays vs. Brewers
Enjoying Covers content? Add us as a preferred source on your Google account
2026 World Series prediction: Brewers moneyline
The Milwaukee Brewers are 62% favorites in the latest World Series odds, and have several statistical advantages over the Tampa Bay Rays that could decide this series.
For starters, Milwaukee posted a higher wOBA and xwOBA than Tampa Bay against both left- and right-handed pitching during the regular season. The gap was especially pronounced against lefties, with the Rays ranking 27th in wOBA and 29th in xwOBA.
That trend has continued in the postseason; only the gap has widened further.
The Brewers have posted a .325 wOBA and a .334 xwOBA compared with the Rays' .289 and .287.
Milwaukee also has the home-field advantage, with Games 1 and 2 at American Family Field, and Games 6 and 7 there, if necessary.
The Brewers went 55-26 at home and ranked third in wOBA, while the Rays went a mere 43-38 on the road and ranked 16th in wOBA.
Milwaukee has another huge organizational edge: Tampa Bay starters Drew Rasmussen and Freddy Peralta both made their MLB debuts with the Brewers.
The Brewers' familiarity with Rasmussen and Peralta will be the final piece of the Brew Crew's championship puzzle.
2026 MLB World Series MVP prediction: Jacob Misiorowski
If there's any question about who the best pitcher in baseball is, there won’t be after the World Series.
Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski — trading at 13% in the World Series MVP odds at Polymarket — has held opposing hitters to a minuscule .248 wOBA and .052 ISO across 20 1/3 postseason innings. He held batters to a league-low .226 xwOBA during the regular season.
Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy has benefited from Misiorowski throwing just 182 pitches across 8 1/3 innings in the Brewers' first two rounds of the 2026 playoffs. Milwaukee's go-to righty will be fully rested and available for multiple starts — and potential relief appearances — if the series goes long enough against Tampa Bay.
Misiorowski will start Game 1 on 11 days' rest. The Brewers carefully managed his workload during the regular season, limiting the NL Cy Young favorite to just 174 2/3 innings over his 30 starts.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] World Series Preview: Who are the Brewers?

item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays — the top team in the American League — has held its own to achieve the third pennant in franchise history, and their second this decade.
The Milwaukee Brewers are back in the World Series for the first time since 1982, and they're doing it as the National League's best team. The 103-win Crew swept the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS and now host the Tampa Bay Rays in a matchup of two franchise-first title seekers. Game 1 is Friday at American Family Field.
Here's a position-by-position look at the Brewers as they prepare for the Rays.
Catcher
William Contreras is the lead backstop for Milwaukee, and one of the most popular Brewers, as he has been one of the more reliable all-around catchers in the National League in recent years and in the playoffs, as his bat has stayed productive into October. He posted a strong 1.157 OPS with three homers through the NLCS while handling a staff that mixes elite velocity with a deep lefty presence.
At backup, the more familiar Gary Sánchez provides a power-oriented option off the bench.
Infield
The Brewers' infield blends elite defense, speed, and opportunistic offense.
- First base: Jake Bauers. The NLCS MVP has been the postseason story for Milwaukee. A well-known Rays prospect if you've read this site for any length of time, Bauers nearly retired but returned for what he considered one more season last year to keep his health insurance benefits after his wife became pregnant with their second child. Fast forward two seasons, and he has delivered lengthy at bats with power and timely hitting throughout October while providing solid enough defense at the corner. Veteran White Sox infielder Andrew Vaughn has also seen time at first and as a right-handed bat off the bench or at DH against lefties.
- Second base: Brice Turang. One of the best all-around second basemen in baseball and the No. 2 hitter. Turang combines Gold Glove-caliber defense with improved power (21 home runs and 100 RBIs in the regular season) and baserunning. He's a clear mismatch advantage and not to be trifled with.
- Shortstop: Cooper Pratt. The 22-year old rookie shortstop has started the bulk of the postseason games. He's shown a contact-oriented approach and improving glove work as the year has progressed, and pushing the previous starter Ortiz into a third base platoon.
- Third base: Joey Ortiz / David Hamilton. This has been a platoon/mix-and-match spot. The right handed hitting Ortiz and left handed hitting Hamilton now split time depending on matchups. If we are drawing comparisons, neither matches Junior Caminero's power, but both offer speed and defensive flexibility that fits Milwaukee's style.
Outfield
Milwaukee's outfield is built on athleticism, defense, and a rising star.
- Left field: Jackson Chourio. This 22-year-old superstar has continued his rapid ascent in 2026. Already with multiple 20-20 seasons under his belt, Chourio brings power, speed, and improving defense. He's the dynamic centerpiece of the lineup, their version of a Junior Caminero, and fun to watch.
- Center field: Garrett Mitchell. Strong defensive center fielder who has delivered several big hits in the playoffs, including a go-ahead home run in the NLCS clincher. He gets on base and covers ground.
- Right field: Sal Frelick. Elite defender with speed and contact skills. Luis Lara has spelled him against left-handers and provides another athletic option. The group ranks among the best defensive outfields in the league.
Technically also an outfielder, the Designated Hitter, Christian Yelich, remains in the lineup and was recently named club captain. While not at his peak production levels, his experience and ability to still impact games remain valuable, especially against right-handed pitching.
Rotation
Manager Pat Murphy has utilized short leashes and heavy bullpen support, but has a solid rotation heading into the World Series:
- Jacob Misiorowski — The clear ace and yet to be crowned NL Cy Young winner (16-5, 1.80 ERA, 252 strikeouts in the regular season). He's started Game 1 of both the NLDS and NLCS and will surely open the World Series. To say his high-velocity stuff that ranks among the best is an understatement. I half expected Misiorowski to mean fast in Polish, but apparently it's something closer to bear.
- Logan Henderson — The reliable No. 2. Solid second-half performer who has handled Game 2 duties effectively in his sophomore season as a homegrown talent.
- Robert Gasser — Emerged as the preferred Game 3 option after strong late-season form and solid postseason outings (including shutout work in the NLCS). He was acquired in the Josh Hader trade with San Diego, over came a UCL surgery in 2025, and started the year in Triple-A, making his rise a bit unexpected. His dad's best friend is evidently Vin Diesel.
- Dustin May (with Shane Drohan as an Opener) — May has postseason experience but has been used carefully; Florida State alumni Drohan opened Game 4 in the NLCS, and the southpaw seems likely to get the nod again given how well that went last time.
No starter has gone particularly deep in October, which is by design. Milwaukee trusts its relievers to take over after four or five innings, limiting any time-through-the-order penalties.
Bullpen
This unit has been the difference-maker. The Brewers' bullpen allowed just six earned runs across more than 40 postseason innings heading into the World Series and featured relievers earning the win in all four NLCS games during the sweep of Los Angeles.
- Trevor Megill — 6'8" Closer. Reliable late-inning presence, and a bit of an invention by the Brewers, having been added for a PTBNL in April 2023.
- Abner Uribe — Primary setup man. High-velocity right-hander who has been outstanding, despite blowing a save in Game 3 of the NLCS he's been their best bullpen arm this month.
- Aaron Ashby — Left-handed workhorse who has been nearly unhittable in October (multiple scoreless multi-inning outings) and got the save in Game 4 of the sweep.
- DL Hall / JoJo Romero — Additional lefty depth options that each were credited wins in the NLCS.
Regular season starter Kyle Harrison will likely find his way into the mix as well. The group throws exceptionally hard on average and enters the series fully rested after the NLCS sweep and the Rays' longer ALCS.
Conclusion
The Brewers' formula is clear: elite defense, contact and speed on offense, an electric frontline starter, and a lights-out bullpen that can cover the middle and late innings.
Against a similarly constructed Rays team that also emphasizes pitching, defense, and small-ball elements, the series should be tight, low-scoring, and decided by the margins. Milwaukee holds home-field advantage and the deeper, harder-throwing relief corps—two factors that could prove decisive in a first-time-champion showdown.

item.title: [PCMag] Milwaukee Brewers vs. Tampa Bay Rays Livestream: How to Watch This Week's World Series Game 1, Even for Free
item.dc:creator: Jason Cohen
item.description: The MLB World Series is finally here after several weeks of intense playoff action. The Brewers swept the Dodgers to reach the World Series for the first time in 44 years. The Rays beat out the Guardians in six games to win the American League pennant for just the third time. Whoever wins, this will be the franchise's first championship. Which team will come out on top? Here's how you can watch every World Series Game live, and even for free. What Time Is the Milwaukee Brewers vs. Tampa Bay Rays
item.content:encoded:
The MLB World Series is finally here after several weeks of intense playoff action. The Brewers swept the Dodgers to reach the World Series for the first time in 44 years. The Rays beat out the Guardians in six games to win the American League pennant for just the third time. Whoever wins, this will be the franchise's first championship.
Which team will come out on top? Here's how you can watch every World Series Game live, and even for free.
What Time Is the Milwaukee Brewers vs. Tampa Bay Rays Game?
Game 1 between the Rays and Brewers will take place on Friday, October 23 at 8:00 p.m. ET.
How to Watch the Milwaukee Brewers vs. Tampa Bay Rays?
This year, the World Series will be broadcast on Fox and the Fox One app. You can also watch it with a live TV or sports streaming subscription from DirecTV, Fubo, Hulu, Sling, Sportsnet+ (if you're in Canada), or YouTube TV.
How to Watch the Brewers vs. Rays for Free
If you don't want to subscribe to any of the above platforms, you may be able to sign up for a few free trials to gain access to the remaining games. Fox One and Hulu offer three-day trials, DirecTV and Fubo offer five days, and YouTube TV gives you 10 days for free.
2026 MLB World Series Game Schedule
MLB's expanded postseason means more teams on the playoff schedule. In the Wild Card round, the Braves beat the Phillies, the Padres beat the Cubs, the Yankees defeated the Red Sox, and the White Sox defeated the Astros. The winners advanced to the Division Series, where the Los Angeles Dodgers, Milwaukee Brewers, Tampa Bay Rays, and Cleveland Guardians beat their respective opponents.
For the Championship Series, the Brewers beat the Dodgers in four games to clinch the National League pennant. The Rays defeated the Guardians in six games to capture the American League pennant. Now, Milwaukee and Tampa Bay will face off in the best-of-seven World Series to begin on October 23. Who will get to raise the trophy?
World Series: Milwaukee Brewers vs. Tampa Bay Rays
- Game 1 on October 23 - Fox/Fox One
- Game 2 on October 24 - Fox/Fox One
- Game 3 on October 26 - Fox/Fox One
- Game 4 on October 27 - Fox/Fox One
- Game 5 on October 28 - Fox/Fox One*
- Game 6 on October 30 - Fox/Fox One*
- Game 7 on October 31 - Fox/Fox One*
*if necessary
How to Stream the 2026 MLB Playoffs
This year's MLB postseason is stretched across multiple networks and streaming services. All Wild Card Series games for the American League and National League were broadcast on NBC, NBCSN, and Peacock. ALDS and ALCS games were on TBS/TruTV and HBO Max, while NLDS and NLCS games were on Fox/FS1. For the World Series, all games will be broadcast on Fox and the Fox One streaming service.
- DirecTV: DirecTV's MySports base pack costs $45 per month for the first six months to see every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, and TBS/TruTV.
- Fox One: Fox's own streaming app lets you watch the NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox and FS1 for $20 per month.
- Fubo: Fubo's Sports plan costs $45.99 for the first month to watch the Wild Card Series, NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox, FS1, and NBC/NBCSN.
- HBO Max: If you pay for the $18.49-per-month HBO Max Standard, you'll be able to watch the ALDS and ALCS games on TBS/TruTV.
- Hulu: For $90 per month, you can watch every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, TBS, and TruTV.
- Peacock: Instead of a live TV service, you'd need to pay $10.99 per month for Peacock Premium to see the Wild Card Series games.
- Sling: The $60.99-per-month Sling Orange & Blue bundle will let you watch the ALDS and ALCS on TBS/TruTV and the NLDS and NLCS on FS1. Day Passes are also available for Sling Orange, allowing you to watch games on TBS for up to seven days.
- Sportsnet+ (Canada only): The $30-per-month Standard tier lets you watch every postseason game.
- YouTube TV: Though the standard plan for YouTube TV costs $83 per month, you can actually now pay for the cheaper $65 Sports package to see all games on Fox, FS1, NBC/NBCSN, and TBS/TruTV.
Can I Watch Postseason Games on MLB.TV?
Are you already an MLB.TV subscriber? You can watch the Division Series, Championship Series, and World Series games through MLB's own streaming service—but there's a catch. To watch on MLB.TV, you'll first need to authenticate through a participating pay TV provider. It's such a sticking point that it makes the entire question moot. If you already have a TV provider, then you wouldn't need to use a streaming service. If you don't already have an MLB.TV subscription, don't pay for one now.
How can I listen to the 2026 postseason?
You can also listen to the games via ESPN Radio.
Which Teams Are In the Playoffs?
Since MLB expanded its postseason picture in 2022, a total of 12 teams make the playoffs each year. That includes six teams per league, including the three division winners and three Wild Card teams.
- American League Division Winners: Tampa Bay Rays (1), Cleveland Guardians (2), Houston Astros (3)
- American League Wild Card: New York Yankees (4), Boston Red Sox (5), Chicago White Sox (6)
- National League Division Winners: Milwaukee Brewers (1), Los Angeles Dodgers (2), Atlanta Braves (3)
- National League Wild Card: Chicago Cubs (4), Philadelphia Phillies (5), San Diego Padres (6)
Upgrade Your Streaming Experience
If you decide to watch the MLB postseason, there's still time to get a big-screen television for viewing this beautiful game. Pro tip: Turn on your TV's motion-smoothing option for the best picture while watching sports. Just remember to turn it off before watching other TV shows and movies to avoid the awful "soap opera" effect.
About Our Expert
As PCMag's editor of how to content, I have to cover a wide variety of topics and also make our stories accessible to everyday users. Considering my history as a technical writer, copywriter, and all-around freelancer covering baseball, comics, and more at various outlets, I am used to making myself into an expert.
I believe tech corporations are bad, but you might as well know how to use technology in everyday life. Want more how to content delivered right to your inbox? Sign up for the tips and tricks newsletter that I curate three times a week.
My job as how-to guru means I use just about every gadget under the sun, so I can figure out how everything works. I work from a Lenovo ThinkPad running Windows 11, but also have a very large Dell Inspiron 17 3000 and Apple silicon MacBook. I have a Google Pixel 6a for personal use and use a Galaxy Z Flip 4 for additional Samsung-related testing. For iOS coverage, an iPhone 13 mini works like a charm, though it's already becoming a little long in the tooth.
My desktop situation includes a dual monitor setup with a modest Acer monitor. I also use a Logitech vertical mouse (who can use these ThinkPad trackpads) and a Havit keyboard (my first mechanical keyboard; I love it but my wife hates it!). I'm a recent convert from wired headphones; I have Anker Soundcore Liberty Air wireless earbuds for personal use and have taken to the Sennheiser HD 450BT headphones for work.
Whenever I have a second to myself, I'm probably gaming on my Nintendo Switch 2, Steam Deck, or Xbox Series S. I also still have a bunch of classic consoles lying around as well.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers Fans Name Their Biggest Threat to Re-Signing Tarik Skubal
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have their work cut out for them this offseason after being swept in the National League Championship Series, but item No. 1 on that to-do list likely involves ace pitcher Tarik Skubal. Skubal may have joined the Dodgers just ahead of the trade deadline, but in his limited appearances, he was as good as advertised. How did Tarik Skubal play for the Dodgers in 2026? item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have their work cut out for them this offseason after being swept in the National League Championship Series, but item No. 1 on that to-do list likely involves ace pitcher Tarik Skubal.
Skubal may have joined the Dodgers just ahead of the trade deadline, but in his limited appearances, he was as good as advertised.
How did Tarik Skubal play for the Dodgers in 2026?
In the regular season, Skubal started 10 games for the Dodgers, putting up a 5-2 record and 2.61 ERA in that span, per Baseball Reference.
He also had a strong outing in the National League Division Series, throwing six innings of one-run ball with two hits allowed, two walks and seven strikeouts.
The NLCS, though, was a little trickier, giving up a pair of runs in five innings of work. He struck out seven batters while allowing five hits and two walks.
It's not as if Skubal's struggles made him an outlier, though, as no Dodgers pitcher was able to get a win against the Milwaukee Brewers.
Seeing as he did all of this just months after recovering from elbow surgery, teams are lining up to try to land the free agent, who's predicted to get a deal somewhere in the neighborhood of eight years and $355 million, according to Kiley McDaniel of ESPN.
Where will Tarik Skubal play in 2027?
With a contract expected to be that large, many assume that the Dodgers will be the favorites to land Skubal on another deal.
There are plenty of other suitors, though, including his former team, the Detroit Tigers, a squad he's previously said he'd like to return to.
Some of our readers here at Dodgers Nation have referenced that moment when making predictions.
"If tigers can come up with the money he'll go back to Detroit since he never wanted to leave in the first place. Otherwise it'll be between the Dodgers and mets," wrote @l.a._dougq8.
"I truly believe it's between the Dodgers or the Tigers for Skubal. I can see the Padres trying to go in for him but I don't see him landing there," aded @austinmandy_.
Plenty of Dodgers fans said they hope Skubal comes back for another season at Chavez Ravine, but some more pragmatic readers put it plainly.
"Hes going to a team that spends the most on him. Bet on it," wrote @abee76.
Where do you think Tarik Skubal will end up?

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] After Nearly a Decade, Christian Yelich Is Finally Getting a Title Shot
item.dc:creator: Shaun McAvoy
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers have been the definition of sustained success over the last nine years, reaching the postseason eight times, but after a sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers, they have finally reached the World Series. Milwaukee has won its division in each of the past four seasons and six times in total over the last nine years, but despite its consistent talent, it has not reached the World Series until now. The Brewers have been dominant for nearly a decade, a stretch that coincides with th
item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers have been the definition of sustained success over the last nine years, reaching the postseason eight times, but after a sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers, they have finally reached the World Series.
Milwaukee has won its division in each of the past four seasons and six times in total over the last nine years, but despite its consistent talent, it has not reached the World Series until now. The Brewers have been dominant for nearly a decade, a stretch that coincides with the arrival of superstar Christian Yelich.
Yelich, 34, quickly became the face of the Brewers organization after winning the National League MVP award in 2018, and he nearly did it again the next season. Though Yelich may not be the same player he used to be, he still has made such an impact that Milwaukee named him the team's first official captain in September. He joins Aaron Judge and Salvador Perez as the only active MLB captains.
Yelich has been the face of the Brewers' franchise for years
"Christian Yelich joined the Milwaukee Brewers following a 2017 trade and quickly became the face of the franchise," Bleacher Report's Erik Beaston wrote on Tuesday. "He won the NL MVP award in 2018 and earned 'captain' status with the organization as its leader, both in front of the cameras and behind the scenes. He has been through the highs and the lows with the team, and while he may not be quite the player he once was, there is no denying that he is as synonymous with this generation of the Milwaukee squad as anyone.
"After a season that saw him deliver 104 hits, 12 home runs, 59 RBI, and a slash line of .235/.315/.378, it will bear watching as to whether or not Yelich still has that superstar magic left in him and can help propel his organization to its first world championship. A close friend of the late Brewers play-by-play announcer, the legendary Bob Uecker, Yelich figures to be playing for teammates both here and gone when he takes to the diamond Friday night at American Family Field."
Yelich has stepped up throughout the postseason, slashing .292/.370/.333 with three RBIs, two walks and three runs scored. After years of leading the Brewers, the 34-year-old is finally getting the chance to play on the biggest stage and potentially help Milwaukee win its first World Series.
Game 1 of the World Series is set for Friday, and Yelich will need to maintain his high level of play if the Brewers want to take down the Tampa Bay Rays.
Shaun McAvoy is a freelance writer with experience working with Newsweek, NESN, The Sporting News and SportsNet Pittsburgh. Shaun is a Boston-area native, growing up in Billerica, Massachusetts, and graduating from Merrimack College with a degree in Sports Management and Communications and Media. Shaun is a massive Star Wars, Marvel and DC fan.
Follow shaunmcavoy3

item.content:encoded:
Juan Soto
had a short message for Freddy Peralta after the Tampa Bay Rays star won the 2026 American League Championship Series (ALCS) MVP award on Monday. The New York Mets outfielder shared two comments on his Instagram story as the Rays beat the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 in Game 6 to reach the World Series. Soto’s words came after Peralta turned his season around following a trade from New York to Tampa Bay in August. The pitcher’s strong playoff run has now earned him one of baseball’s biggest postseason awards.
Juan Soto’s Instagram Messages Follow Freddy Peralta’s ALCS MVP Award
Soto shared two messages in Spanish on his Instagram story on Monday. One read, “Did I tell you so or what?” The second said, “the best in the classroom 🔥,” according to the English translations provided.
The comments came on the same day Peralta received the ALCS MVP award after helping Tampa Bay win the series against Cleveland. The Rays took the series 4-2 and claimed their third American League pennant. They last reached the World Series in 2020.
Peralta was once Soto’s teammate with the Mets. However, New York traded the right-handed pitcher to Tampa Bay on August 2 after a difficult first part of the season.
Soto had his own challenges in 2026. The five-time All-Star hit .275 with 27 home runs but missed several games because of a calf strain.
His brief messages put the focus on Peralta’s big achievement, which came after a major change in teams and a much stronger finish to the season.
How Freddy Peralta Turned His Season Around With the Tampa Bay Rays
Peralta struggled during his time with the Mets. He went 5-9 with a 4.99 ERA across 22 starts in New York. After joining Tampa Bay, he recorded a 3.25 ERA over his final 10 regular-season starts, giving the Rays a much stronger option on the mound.
His work against Cleveland in the ALCS was even better. Peralta finished with a 0.75 ERA, nine strikeouts and just one run allowed over 12 innings. He won twice and also made a short relief appearance during the series.
In Game 6 on Monday, Peralta allowed one run over 5 1/3 innings as Tampa Bay secured a 7-3 victory at Tropicana Field. His performance helped the Rays finish off the Guardians and book their place in the World Series.
After receiving the award, Peralta summed up his feelings in a few words.
“This is crazy,” he said, before thanking the people around him.
“I’m very happy to be here, to be part of this great group and this organization. Milwaukee is always going to be in my heart, but it’s time to compete.”
The Associated Press and MLB.com reported on Peralta’s reaction after the game. CBS Sports also reported his ALCS MVP win and his strong postseason performance.
Peralta spent his first eight seasons with the Milwaukee Brewers before moving to the Mets in January. New York then traded him to Tampa Bay in August. Now, he will face his former Milwaukee team in the World Series.
The matchup gives Peralta a chance to compete for a championship against the club where he began his major league career. For the Rays, his late-season improvement has helped carry them to baseball’s biggest stage.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Mets acquired Freddy Peralta from the Milwaukee Brewers in the offseason, hoping he could be their ace.
Peralta was a two-time All-Star with the Brewers, but struggled in Queens. He had a 4.99 ERA in 22 starts for the Mets and was traded to the Tampa Bay Rays. With the Rays, he got back on track, posting a 0.79 ERA in his final six regular-season starts and winning the American League Championship Series MVP Award.
Even though Peralta did not pitch well for the Mets, he seemingly made a strong impression on his teammates. Juan Soto sent a message on Instagram about Peralta after he won the ALCS MVP.
"The best in the room…didn't I tell you," he wrote in Spanish on his Instagram story.
Peralta has always been regarded as a great teammate and as someone who has a joyful energy. Even after he was traded from the Mets, he thanked fans, teammates and the Mets organization for giving him a chance.
Peralta will now have a chance to pitch in the World Series for the first time in his career, and will get to do so against the team that developed him into a star pitcher. After that, he is set up for a major payday in free agency.

item.content:encoded:
Cronograma de la Serie Mundial 2026 de la MLB Rays vs Brewers: fechas, hora en CDMX y canal donde ver el juego
La serie se disputará al mejor de siete encuentros y tendrá un atractivo especial: el ganador conseguirá el primer título de Serie Mundial en la historia de su franquicia
La Serie Mundial 2026 ya tiene a sus dos protagonistas. Los Tampa Bay Rays vencieron 7-3 a los Cleveland Guardians en el sexto juego de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Americana y sellaron su boleto al Clásico de Otoño, donde enfrentarán a los Milwaukee Brewers, que eliminaron por barrida a los Los Angeles Dodgers.
La final de las Grandes Ligas de Beisbol comenzará este viernes 23 de octubre en Milwaukee. La serie se disputará al mejor de siete encuentros y tendrá un atractivo especial: el ganador conseguirá el primer título de Serie Mundial en la historia de su franquicia.
The Rays and Brewers are both vying for their first World Series championship! It's the first time since 1980 (Phillies vs. Royals) where both teams in the Fall Classic are seeking their first title https://t.co/sVuhbJAk1H
— MLB (@MLB) October 20, 2026
¿Cuándo empieza la Serie Mundial 2026?
Los Brewers recibirán los dos primeros encuentros en el American Family Field. Después, la serie viajará a Florida para los juegos 3, 4 y 5, mientras que Milwaukee será local nuevamente si la final necesita llegar a los últimos dos partidos.
El calendario contempla siete posibles encuentros, aunque los juegos 5, 6 y 7 solo se disputarán si son necesarios.
ESTO TE INTERESA: ¡Llegó el Clásico de Otoño! ¿Cómo se jugará la Serie Mundial 2026? Días, sedes y rivales confirmados
Calendario de la Serie Mundial: fechas y horarios
Estos son los horarios para Ciudad de México, de acuerdo con el calendario oficial de MLB. Todos los encuentros están programados para las 18:00 horas.
- Juego 1: viernes 23 de octubre, en Milwaukee
- Juego 2: sábado 24 de octubre, en Milwaukee
- Juego 3: lunes 26 de octubre, en Tampa Bay
- Juego 4: martes 27 de octubre, en Tampa Bay
- Juego 5: miércoles 28 de octubre, en Tampa Bay, si es necesario
- Juego 6: viernes 30 de octubre, en Milwaukee, si es necesario
- Juego 7: sábado 31 de octubre, en Milwaukee, si es necesario
La transmisión de los partidos en México estará a cargo de Televisa Deportes por Canal 9 en tv abierta; ESPN y FOX también tendrán transmisiones.
TAMBIÉN PUEDES LEER: ¡Muere el rey! Dodgers queda eliminado con barrida de los Brewers que van a la Serie Mundial
Las figuras latinas que buscarán el título
La Serie Mundial también tendrá presencia latinoamericana. Entre los jugadores destacados de Milwaukee figuran el venezolano William Contreras, el dominicano Abner Uribe y el jardinero venezolano Jackson Chourio.
Por Tampa Bay sobresalen el mexicano Jonathan Aranda, los cubanos Yandy Díaz y Víctor Mesa Jr., además de los dominicanos Freddy Peralta y Junior Caminero.
Precisamente, Caminero y Díaz conectaron cuadrangulares de dos carreras en el sexto juego ante Cleveland. Peralta, por su parte, fue reconocido como el Jugador Más Valioso de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Americana, después de contribuir de manera decisiva a la clasificación de los Rays.
TE RECOMENDAMOS: ¡Lista, la serie Mundial 2026! Rays vence a Guardians y se cita con los Brewers en la lucha por el título; ¿cuándo y dónde comienza?
Con dos equipos que buscan conquistar por primera vez el campeonato, la Serie Mundial 2026 promete una final histórica para Milwaukee y Tampa Bay.

item.title: [abc7.com] Where 2026 ranks among best World Series matchups since 2000
item.dc:creator: David Schoenfield
item.description: This year's World Series will have a tough act to follow. Not only was the 2025 World Series between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Toronto Blue Jays the first seven-game affair since 2019, but it featured an 18-inning game and then a Game 7 that might have been the greatest baseball game ever played. The good news is we're guaranteed that a long-starved fanbase will get to celebrate in 2026. The Milwaukee Brewers, coming off their impressive and dynamic four-game sweep of the Dodgers in the NLCS,
item.content:encoded:
This year's World Series will have a tough act to follow. Not only was the 2025 World Series between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Toronto Blue Jays the first seven-game affair since 2019, but it featured an 18-inning game and then a Game 7 that might have been the greatest baseball game ever played.
The good news is we're guaranteed that a long-starved fanbase will get to celebrate in 2026. The Milwaukee Brewers, coming off their impressive and dynamic four-game sweep of the Dodgers in the NLCS, are in the Fall Classic for the first time since 1982 and seek the first championship in franchise history, looking to put an exclamation point on their season after leading the majors with 103 wins.
The Tampa Bay Rays were a 1998 expansion franchise and reached the World Series in 2008 and 2020 (the shortened season during the COVID-19 pandemic) but are seeking their first title as well. Young power hitter Junior Caminero and unheralded staff ace Drew Rasmussen lead the way as the Rays look to finally cash in after making the playoffs six times in the past eight seasons.
The Brewers and Rays led their respective leagues in wins, always a bonus for those who want the best teams in the World Series. Of course, a lot of attention will be given to the small-market aspect of the matchup, as the cloud of the lockout looms in the offseason.
Let's rank all the World Series since 2000 to see where Brewers-Rays fits in. This ranking is based on hype, the quality of the teams and their star power heading into the World Series. It's not a ranking of the quality of the World Series itself, although we're going to include a grade on that for each matchup. Let's get to it.
The Yankees were back in the World Series for the sixth time in eight years, and the Marlins had rebuilt after their fire sale following their World Series title in 1997. Trust me when I say that nobody wanted the Yankees in the World Series yet again. And the Marlins were merely a 91-win wild-card team. Most notably, however, both teams had spoiled the ultimate World Series by knocking off the Cubs and Red Sox -- before either team had overcome its curse -- in Game 7s in the LCS.
Actual World Series: C. The Marlins won Game 4 in 12 innings, when Yankees manager Joe Torre inexplicably failed to use reliever Mariano Rivera, and then 23-year-old Josh Beckett tossed a five-hit shutout in Game 6.
In an all-wild-card series, the fifth-seeded Rangers had won 90 games and the sixth-seeded Diamondbacks won only 84, making this the lowest combined win total in World Series history (for full seasons). The Rangers were going for their first World Series title, so there was that, and there were some fun hitters -- Corey Seager, the red-hot Adolis Garcia (who had just driven in 15 runs in the ALCS) and Corbin Carroll -- but it was a soft matchup on paper.
Actual World Series: D-. The series turned on Seager's tying two-run homer off Paul Sewald in the bottom of the ninth of Game 1, which Garcia then won with a home run in the 11th. There wasn't a single lead change after that, and three of those games were blowouts.
This was the Cardinals team that got hot in September and clinched a wild-card spot on the final day of the season when the Braves blew a lead in the ninth inning and lost in extra innings. St. Louis certainly had star power with the likes of Albert Pujols, Lance Berkman and Matt Holliday but had won a World Series fairly recently (2006), and the Rangers had just been there the year before.
Actual World Series: A. The first two games were one-run games, including the Rangers pulling out a victory with two runs in the ninth. In Game 3, Pujols blasted a record-tying three home runs. Game 6 was the David Freese Game -- perhaps the single most exciting baseball game ever played. Game 7 was a bit of an anticlimactic 6-2 Cardinals win.
The second-lowest combined win total in World Series history featured two wild-card teams that won fewer than 90 games. The Royals were at least a good story -- in the playoffs for the first time since winning the World Series in 1985 -- and had gone 8-0 in the AL playoffs, including an epic win over the A's in the wild-card game. The Giants, however, had just won the World Series in 2010 and 2012, and this team didn't seem nearly as good as those two.
Actual World Series: B-. Five of the games were blowouts, but it did at least go seven. It'll be remembered for Madison Bumgarner's historic performance: a shutout in Game 5 (the last complete game shutout in World Series history) and then five scoreless innings of relief in Game 7, getting Salvador Perez to pop out with the tying run on third to end it.
The Red Sox were only three years removed from breaking the Curse of the Bambino in 2004, so although they were still a star-laden team with David Ortiz, Manny Ramirez and scrappy rookie Dustin Pedroia, they were no longer as interesting. The Rockies were a fun story, winning 14 of their final 15 games, including beating the Padres in a tiebreaker, just to win a wild-card spot. Then they went 7-0 in the NL playoffs and had won 21 of 22 entering the World Series.
Actual World Series: F.A dud. Two of the games were one-run games, but this goes down as one of the least memorable World Series of all time, with a forgettable four-game sweep.
The Tigers were the story of the season. They had lost 119 games three years before and 91 just the previous year. With rookie starter Justin Verlander winning 17 games, they led the AL Central most of the season -- only to lose their final five games and squeak into the playoffs as a wild-card team. The Cardinals won a weak NL Central with only 83 wins -- although they at least had Pujols at his absolute peak (.331/.431/.671, 49 home runs). Both teams hadn't won a World Series in a couple of decades: 1982 for the Cardinals, 1984 for the Tigers. Plus, it did feature two of the original 16 franchises.
Actual World Series: F. The Cardinals won one game in the bottom of the eighth, but it was otherwise a blur of nothing, most characterized by several fielding miscues by Tigers pitchers. David Eckstein won MVP honors without hitting a home run and while driving in only four runs.
The Braves were back in the World Series for the first time since 1999 -- they had made 12 playoff appearances in the intervening years without making it to the Fall Classic. Still, this was the weakest of the Atlanta playoff teams of recent vintage, winning only 88 games and missing Ronald Acuña Jr. for the playoffs. The Astros, meanwhile, were back in the World Series for the third time in five years -- but the first time since the 2017 sign-stealing scandal had broken in November 2019. Let's just say not everyone wanted them there.
Actual World Series: D. This was a weird World Series. The Braves ended up going with two bullpen games (who remembers that Dylan Lee and Tucker Davidson started?) after Charlie Morton broke a leg in Game 1. Astros starters kept getting knocked out early (the only starter to go more than five innings for either team was Max Fried in the finale). Four of the games were blowouts.
The Giants were back after winning in 2010, and the Tigers were back for the first time since 2006, featuring Triple Crown winner Miguel Cabrera and a strong 1-2 punch in the rotation with Verlander and Max Scherzer. This was also the last World Series with that season's MVP winners until Aaron Judge and Shohei Ohtani in 2024, with Cabrera and Buster Posey.
Actual World Series: D-. A boring sweep. Pablo Sandoval did hit three home runs in Game 1, but there were two shutouts and chilly weather in Detroit made the final two games unbearable.
This one did feature the two best teams from the regular season (both won 97 games), the last time before this year that we had that happen in a full season. It was also a classic original-16 matchup, although we had seen this in 2004 -- plus, both teams had won recently (2007 for Boston, 2011 for St. Louis). These were veteran teams, with Ortiz leading the Red Sox and the Cardinals featuring four .300 hitters, plus Carlos Beltran, who hit .296 and led the team in home runs.
Actual World Series: C+. Ortiz was absolutely locked in, hitting .688/.760/1.188 with two home runs and eight walks. The Cardinals were so scared of him by Game 6 that they intentionally walked him three times -- with two of those helping lead to rallies and a 6-1 Red Sox victory in the final game.
This one could be No. 25 -- it was during the pandemic, after all, and it was played at a neutral site in a half-empty stadium for social distancing reasons. But it was a great matchup between the teams with the best records in each league, albeit over the shortened 60-game season. You had Mookie Betts and Clayton Kershaw and Randy Arozarena in the midst of one of the best postseasons ever, plus the small-market Rays trying to beat the big-market Dodgers.
Actual World Series: C+. Because teams were allowed an expanded roster of 28 players, it was a parade of relievers -- but there were some fun games, including a bonkers ending to Game 4 and then Rays manager Kevin Cash's controversial decision to remove Blake Snell in Game 6, which backfired in a big way.
Maybe this should rate higher. After all, at the time, the White Sox were trying to break a World Series drought going back to 1917 and the Astros, born in 1962, had never won. But the White Sox's drought never had the same nationwide interest as the ones for the Cubs or Red Sox (fair or not) and these weren't particularly interesting teams. The White Sox were very good -- they won 99 games -- but lacked star power, with Paul Konerko their biggest name (Frank Thomas was on the team that year but played only 34 games and was injured for the playoffs). The Astros had Yankees transplants Roger Clemens and Andy Pettitte, but their two longtime stars, Jeff Bagwell and Craig Biggio, were at the end of their careers (Bagwell, in his final season, was relegated to DH and pinch-hitting duties).
Actual World Series: C. It's hard to give a sweep a decent grade, but all four games were exciting, including Scott Podsednik's walk-off home run in Game 2 (after not hitting a home run all season) and Geoff Blum's go-ahead home run in the 14th inning to win Game 3.
The Phillies were back in the World Series for the first time since 1993 -- and hadn't won since 1980. They featured a powerful offense with Chase Utley, Ryan Howard, Jimmy Rollins and Pat Burrell. The Rays were maybe the unlikeliest World Series team ever: In their 10 previous years of existence, they had not only never had a winning season but had lost at least 90 games in each one. They won 97 games that year behind rookie Evan Longoria and power-hitting first baseman Carlos Peña, with speedsters Carl Crawford and B.J. Upton in the outfield.
Actual World Series: D+. Three games were decided by one run, but it was a pretty uneventful World Series. The lasting memory is the cold and rain in Philly that forced the midgame postponement of Game 5, the only time that has happened in World Series history. The game was suspended in the sixth inning and resumed two days later.
A Subway Series -- the first since the Yankees and Brooklyn Dodgers met in 1956 -- was certainly fun for the Big Apple, but it was less fun for the rest of the country (it drew the worst TV ratings at the time). The Yankees were going for a third straight World Series and had officially become the Evil Empire by that point. To make it even worse, they weren't even that good that season, winning only 87 games. The Mets were back in the World Series for the first time since 1986. There was certainly plenty of star power all around with the likes of Derek Jeter, Roger Clemens and Mike Piazza.
Actual World Series: C+. It was a tight-fought five-game series with all games decided by two runs or fewer. The turning point was the bottom of the ninth of Game 1, when the Yankees tied it off Armando Benitez and went on to win in 12 innings. Game 2 featured the infamous Clemens-Piazza bat-throwing incident, and the Yankees won the clincher with two runs in the ninth off a tired Al Leiter.
I know, the Astros ... again. Boo. But this was an absolute powerhouse of a team with 106 wins and stars such asYordan Alvarez (1.019 OPS) and Verlander (18-4, 1.75 ERA), plus the old standbys Jose Altuve and Alex Bregman. The Phillies, meanwhile, snuck in as a wild-card team for their first playoff trip since 2011 but were an immensely entertaining team with Bryce Harper, Kyle Schwarber& Co., as well as a passionate fanbase cheering them on.
Actual World Series: C. The Phillies won 6-5 in Game 1 on J.T. Realmuto's home run in the 10th inning. They took a 2-1 series lead, but then their bats died. Astros pitchers tossed a combined no-hitter to even the series, and Houston won the final two games 3-2 and 4-1, with Alvarez's three-run blast in Game 6 the deciding blow.
The Brewers' drought is the big narrative here as they try to finally cash in after their past decade of success, but we're still getting the 103-win Brewers facing the 98-win Rays, the best combined win total in the World Series since the Astros and Dodgers in 2017. (Not to mention we get a first-time winner no matter the outcome.) The Brewers aren't your conventional powerhouse team -- relying on speed, defense, timely hitting and a dominant bullpen -- but they do have one of the biggest stars of the 2026 season in Jacob Misiorowski, plus a rising star in young Jackson Chourio. The Rays might lack big names, although Junior Caminero is just the second player with two 40-homer seasons by age 22, and like the Brewers, they're trying to finally win it all after years of success.
Actual World Series: To be determined.
The Royals proved their 2014 World Series appearance was no fluke, winning 95 games with a better team that included trade deadline additions Ben Zobrist and Johnny Cueto. The Mets won the NL East behind a young, powerful rotation that featured Matt Harvey, Noah Syndergaard and Jacob deGrom. It was a fun matchup of teams trying to avoid lengthy title droughts -- 30 years for the Royals, 29 for the Mets.
Actual World Series: C+. It went only five games, but the Royals won the opener in 14 innings, won Game 5 with a three-run eighth inning and then won the clincher in 12 innings -- after Mets manager Terry Collins' ill-fated decision to leave in Harvey to start the ninth with a 2-0 lead.
This was a super entertaining showdown at the time. The Giants had yet to win a World Series in San Francisco and featured Tim Lincecum ("The Freak," for his small stature and overpowering stuff) and two rookies named Posey and Bumgarner. The Rangers had never won a championship and featured AL MVP Josh Hamilton and veteran DH Vladimir Guerrero. Both teams had pulled off upsets in the LCS, with the Giants beating the Phillies and the Rangers beating the Yankees.
Actual World Series: D. Meh. The Giants won the opener in a blowout as the Rangers made four errors and then tossed shutouts in Games 2 (behind Matt Cain) and 4 (behind Bumgarner). You can test Giants fans by asking them who won World Series MVP honors that year. Answer: Edgar Renteria (he hit .412 with two home runs and six RBIs).
Remember, this happened before the sign-stealing scandal changed how we view this era of the Astros. They had won 107 games behind the pitching duo of Verlander and Gerrit Cole and four players who mashed 30-plus home runs (which didn't even include Alvarez, a rookie that year). The Nationals were a wild-card team that had overcome a 19-31 season start to win 93 games and featured a starting pitching trio of Scherzer, Stephen Strasburg and Patrick Corbin (and 20-year-old sensation Juan Soto, who hit 34 home runs).
Actual World Series: B-. It went seven games -- the road team would win all seven -- although five of the games weren't close. The best game was the last one: The Nationals went ahead 3-2 in the seventh inning on Anthony Rendon's home run and then Howie Kendrick's go-ahead home run just inside the right-field foul pole.
This matchup began with a lot of hype: Shohei Ohtani, coming off his all-time game in the NLCS in which he hit three home runs and struck out 10 batters as the starting pitcher, against Vladimir Guerrero Jr., who had hit .442 with six home runs through the first two rounds of the playoffs. The Dodgers were looking to become the first team with back-to-back titles since the 2000 Yankees and the first NL team since the 1976 Reds. The Blue Jays were back in the World Series for the first time since Joe Carter walked off the Phillies in 1993. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts stirred things up after the NLCS when he said during the postgame celebration, "Let's get four more wins and really ruin baseball" -- a reference to the criticism of the Dodgers' high payroll.
Actual World Series: A+. The Dodgers won Game 3 in 18 innings on Freddie Freeman's walk-off home run, which followed an unlikely four-inning relief performance from Will Klein, the last guy on the Dodgers' staff. The Dodgers went back to Toronto trailing 3-2 but won Game 6 behind Yoshinobu Yamamoto and a crazy game-ending double play.
Game 7 featured two future Hall of Famers starting in Ohtani and Max Scherzer, more on-the-edge-of-your-seat plays than any game in World Series history, Miguel Rojas' unlikely home run in the ninth to tie it, as well as Will Smith's go-ahead one in the 11th -- and finally, Yamamoto pitching in relief to close out the game by inducing a double play with two runners on to win it for the Dodgers. It wasn't quite the greatest World Series overall, but two all-time games made it a classic.
The Angels, who joined the majors in 1961, were making their first World Series appearance, while the Giants, in the Bay Area since 1958, were trying to win their first title since moving from New York. You had Barry Bonds at the height of his unstoppable powers -- and trying to erase his own postseason demons -- while the Angels had a loaded lineup (Troy Glaus, Tim Salmon, Garret Anderson), the Rally Monkey and those deafening ThunderStix (let us pray they never return).
Actual World Series: A. Bonds was a beast, hitting .471/.700/1.294 (yes, that's a 1.994 OPS), but it wasn't enough. This series featured four one-run games, including a wild 11-10 contest and the classic Game 6, when the Angels rallied late from a 5-0 deficit to win 6-5. Game 7 was a drab 4-1 contest (Bonds went a harmless 1-for-3).
The Yankees had missed the playoffs in 2008 for the first time since 1993, so they went out and signed free agents CC Sabathia, Mark Teixeira and A.J. Burnett to add to an already stacked roster that included Jeter, Alex Rodriguez, Robinson Cano, Hideki Matsui, Jorge Posada and Johnny Damon. Whoa. Yes, they were still the Evil Empire. The Phillies, trying to defend their title, had traded for Cliff Lee and then signed Pedro Martinez in July to bolster their rotation.
Actual World Series: C. It could have been a classic battle, but there were no one-run games and Game 6 -- Martinez's final start of his career -- was over early. The crucial contest was Game 4, when the Yankees scored three runs in the ninth off Phillies closer Brad Lidge to win 7-4.
This one presented conflicting emotions. The Yankees were going for an unthinkable fourth straight title, but in the wake of 9/11, there was a "Win it for New York" angle that the Yankees had never encountered. The Diamondbacks, meanwhile, had the big, bad duo of Randy Johnson and Curt Schilling. When asked on the eve of the World Series about the Yankees' mystique and aura, Schilling provided one of the great quips in World Series history: "Mystique and Aura? Those are dancers at a nightclub." The Diamondbacks were not going to be intimidated.
Actual World Series: A+. Four one-run games, including three of the most memorable World Series moments ever: Jeter's Mr. November home run to win Game 4, Scott Brosius' walk-off home run to win Game 5 and then Luis Gonzalez's bloop single to beat the invincible Mariano Rivera in Game 7.
Two of baseball's most historic franchises had never met in a World Series, creating the classic showdown with games in Fenway Park and Dodger Stadium. It doesn't get any better than that. The Red Sox were a 108-win powerhouse -- with AL MVP Mookie Betts leading the way, backed up by J.D. Martinez, who hit .330 with 43 home runs that season. Chris Sale and David Price headlined the rotation. The Dodgers actually had a bit of a down year with 92 wins, but they also weren't lacking in big names, with Manny Machado (a trade deadline acquisition), Yasiel Puig, Matt Kemp, Cody Bellinger and Justin Turner, with Kershaw and rookie Walker Buehler on the pitching side.
Actual World Series: C-. A letdown. The first two games in Fenway were cold and windy. Game 3 was an 18-inning affair -- the longest in World Series history -- but was more of a slog than a game to remember. Game 4 was the best of the series as the Red Sox rallied with nine runs over the final three innings to win 9-6.
This series had it all: dominant teams (both won over 100 games), long World Series title droughts (never for the Astros, 1988 for the Dodgers) and superstars galore (Altuve, Verlander, Carlos Correa, Kershaw, Seager, Bellinger, Yu Darvish). We didn't know at the time that both franchises were just kicking off 100-win dynasties -- let alone what the Astros were doing behind the scenes -- but the anticipation level was off the charts for the first matchup of 100-win teams in the World Series since 1970.
Actual World Series: A-. Game 1, with a start-time temperature of 103 degrees at Dodger Stadium, was a Kershaw 11-strikeout gem. The Astros tied Game 2 in the ninth on Marwin Gonzalez's home run off Kenley Jansen (1.32 ERA that season), both teams scored twice in the 10th, the Astros scored twice in the 11th on George Springer's home run and held on for a 7-6 win. Game 4 featured a five-run rally in the ninth by the Dodgers to win. Game 5 was completely bananas, with the Astros finally winning 13-12 in 10 innings. Game 7 was a letdown though, as the Astros won a 5-1 snoozer in which they scored five runs off Darvish in the first two innings.
As mentioned, what's not to like? Aside from Ohtani and Judge each playing in their first World Series and trying to put a final stamp on their legacy-defining seasons, we hadJuan Soto and Mookie Betts, a suddenly rejuvenated Giancarlo Stanton and a hobbled Freddie Freeman (only raising the drama if he hit well), Gerrit Cole and Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Aside from the history between the clubs, we had both clubs needing to rewrite their recent history: The Yankees, back in the World Series for the first time since 2009, and the Dodgers trying to add a more legitimate championship to the one they won in the COVID-shortened season.
Actual World Series:C+. The Judge-Ohtani showdown was a flop, as Judge hit .222 with one home run and Ohtani hit .105 without a home run or RBI. The series also went just five games, with the Dodgers winning the first three. The series did produce two forever moments, however: Freeman's walk-off, Kirk Gibson-esque grand slam in Game 1 and the Yankees' fifth-inning defensive meltdown in Game 5.
The Red Sox were coming off their never-done-before comeback from down 3-0 to beat the Yankees in the ALCS -- and still had to beat a 105-win Cardinals team that featured Pujols (.331, 46 home runs), Jim Edmonds (.301, 42 home runs) and Scott Rolen (.314, 34 home runs), plus in-season pickup Larry Walker, who had an OPS over 1.000 that year. The Red Sox had their own ridiculous lineup with Ortiz (.301, 41 home runs), Ramirez (.308, 43 home runs) and Damon (.304, 20 home runs) plus a rotation with Schilling and Martinez. It seems inevitable now that Boston was going to win, but that wasn't the case at the time, so the buildup was intense.
Actual World Series: D. Blah. I mean, Red Sox fans will rightfully call it the best World Series ever, but after a sloppy 11-9 Game 1 played in a drizzle at Fenway (the Red Sox won despite committing four errors), the Cardinals never led again.
The Cubs had not only not won since 1908, but they hadn't even been in a World Series since 1945. The Guardians, meanwhile, had the second-longest drought of the original 16 teams, without a title since 1948. That was enough right there to build up the anticipation, but this also rates high because it was two good teams -- Chicago won 104 games while Cleveland won 94. Cubs third baseman Kris Bryant won MVP honors that year and Cleveland was led by 18-game winner Corey Kluber (who would start three times) and young rising stars Francisco Lindor and Jose Ramirez.
Actual World Series: B. The first six games weren't anything too special, but Game 7 was one of the greatest in World Series history. Cleveland tied it on Rajai Davis' three-run homer in the bottom of the eighth, the Cubs scored twice in the 10th -- following a stress-filled rain delay -- and escaped with an 8-7, curse-ending win when Cleveland had to bat little-used Michael Martinez with its season on the line.
]

item.title: [woonsocketcall.com] Brewers-Rays will produce a first-time champion, and maybe the first all-indoor World Series
item.dc:creator: RONALD BLUM
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays will play a Suds vs. Sun World Series that will produce a first-time champion and likely baseball's first all-indoor championship. The best-of-seven showdown between low-payroll pennant winners opens Friday night in Milwaukee. item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays will play a Suds vs. Sun World Series that will produce a first-time champion and likely baseball's first all-indoor championship.
The best-of-seven showdown between low-payroll pennant winners opens Friday night in Milwaukee. It'll be the first World Series between title-less teams since the Philadelphia Phillies defeated the Kansas City Royals in 1980 and just the second since 1910.
One city is known for the television sitcom “ Laverne & Shirley," the home of Harley-Davidson motorcycles, cheeseheads and breweries that have included Miller, Pabst and Schlitz. The other is a vacation destination featuring warm weather, beaches and art museums.
“They’re highly athletic but so are we. I’m excited to see two great teams that play the game a little differently than maybe it’s been played the last decade or so,” Rays manager Kevin Cash said after his team defeated Cleveland in six games for the AL pennant. “We’re going to use our speed. We’re going to bunt when it’s called for. We’ll try to get matchups and I can assure you they’re going to do the same.”
Just five of the current 30 teams have never won a title, with Colorado, San Diego and Seattle also ringless.
“The city is ready. I know that the fans are ready, and I know that we’ll be ready,” said Milwaukee's Jake Bauers, MVP of the four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NL Championship Series.
Milwaukee's Jacob Misiorowski heads the pitchers with his 100 mph-plus heat, and each team features a dynamic 22-year-old anchoring the lineup: Jackson Chourio of the Brewers and Junior Caminero of the Rays. Tampa Bay's Freddy Peralta and Drew Rasmussen could pitch against their former team.
“I don’t know how the people, the fans are going to take it, but I’m happy to be go there,” said Peralta, the ALCS MVP. “I have a lot of people that I love over there, people that care about me and I’m happy to be there and be able to compete together and take a lot of pictures and videos."
The Brewers started as the expansion Seattle Pilots in 1969, then were bought by Bud Selig's group in bankruptcy court and moved to Milwaukee for the 1970 season. The team's only Series trip was a seven-game loss to St. Louis in the 1982 Suds Series, back when the Brewers were in the American League.
Tampa Bay launched as the expansion Devil Rays in 1998 and dropped the “Devil” ahead of the 2008 season. The team's two Series appearances ended with losses to Philadelphia in 2008 and the Dodgers in the pandemic-shortened 2020 season.
Best face each other for 6th time in wild-card era
This will be only the sixth time since the start of the wild-card era in 1995 that teams with the top records in each league meet in the World Series after Atlanta-Cleveland (1995), New York Yankees-Braves (1999), Boston-St. Louis (2013), Dodgers-Rays (2020) and Dodgers-Yankees (2024).
Two low-payroll teams in Series for first time in 35 years
Milwaukee had MLB’s 19th-highest payroll as of Aug. 31. Tampa Bay was 25th.
Not since 1991 had both pennant winners been among the bottom 50% in player spending. Minnesota was 15th among 26 teams when it beat Atlanta (19th) in seven games.
Matchup with a ceiling
Tampa Bay’s ballpark has a fixed roof and Milwaukee’s is retractable — it probably will be closed with game-time temperatures predicted to be in the upper 40s or low 50s.
When all World Series games were played at retractable-roof ballparks in 2020 (Texas) and 2023 (Texas and Arizona), there were three open-air games each year.
The roofs of both ballparks came into play this postseason.
In the ninth inning of Milwaukee’s 3-2 win over the Padres in Game 1 of their NL Division Series, San Diego’s Ty France hit a high drive that appeared it might be headed over the left-field wall for a go-ahead homer until it struck a cable on the retractable roof in Milwaukee.
Two nights later, Yankees rookie Spencer Jones hit a flyball off a catwalk at Tropicana Field that was caught by Rays right fielder Victor Mesa Jr. for an out in the second inning of New York’s 5-2 loss in Game 2 of their AL Division Series.
Common ties
Greg Vaughn, Willy Adames and Matt Garza are the most prominent players with lengthy stretches on both teams, and Bauers made his big league debut with the Rays in 2018.
Brewers president of baseball operations Matt Arnold worked for the Rays for nine years before Milwaukee hired him as an assistant GM in October 2015.
One of baseball's great nicknames
Those 1982 Brewers were known as Harvey's Wallbangers, a nickname given by first baseman Cecil Cooper. The Brewers led the major leagues in home runs under manager Harvey Kuenn and had a roster with five future Hall of Famers: Robin Yount, Paul Molitor, Rollie Fingers, Ted Simmons and Don Sutton.
Haunted hotel?
Various players over the years have claimed The Pfister Hotel, where many teams stay in Milwaukee, is haunted. Opened in 1893, the hotel has Romanesque Revival architecture, and players have claimed to hear spooky noises and footsteps.
If there is a Game 7, it would be played in Milwaukee on Halloween night.
Boss Man
Milwaukee's Pat Murphy, winner of the last two NL Manager of the Year awards, has two tattoos referencing Bruce Springsteen: “No Retreat No Surrender” on his left forearm and “The Boss” on his back.
He first went to a Springsteen concert in 1980 when he was in college, then another when he was coaching at Notre Dame.
“He grew up a Catholic kid in New Jersey. I was a Catholic kid from upstate New York,” the 67-year-old Murphy said. “There’s just so much that resonates with me how he speaks about things.”
Ballpark histories
The 1982 Series was played at Milwaukee County Stadium, home of the Braves from 1953-65 before they moved to Atlanta, and then the Brewers from 1970-2000. This year's championship will be played at American Family Field. Known as Miller Park from 2001-20, the ballpark is adjacent to the County Stadium site. It was host of the 2002 All-Star Game, which ended in a 7-7, 11-inning tie after both teams ran out of pitchers.
Milwaukee's ballpark is known for its Racing Sausages in the middle of the sixth inning, with the Brat, Polish, Italian, Hot Dog and Chorizo competing. It also has the Uecker Seat in the last row of section 422 in the left-field upper deck — it includes a bronze statue of Bob Uecker, the beloved funny man who broadcast Brewers games for 54 seasons until his death last year.
Tampa Bay's home, Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, is on its third name. Known as the Florida Suncoast Dome from 1990-93 and the ThunderDome from 1993-96, the stadium got its current name about 18 months before the Rays' first game in 1998.
Its only prior World Series games were in 2008, when the Rays split the first two games against Philadelphia before the Phillies won three straight at home. Tampa Bay's other Series appearance was in 2020, when due to the coronavirus pandemic the entire series was played at Globe Life Field in Arlington, Texas.
The Trop reopened this season after repairs to damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The Rays plan to move to a new stadium across the bay in Tampa in 2029.
Jersey watch
Milwaukee went 29-13 in cream uniforms during the regular season, 17-7 in pinstripes, 27-12 in navy blue, 9-6 in City Connect outfits and 21-21 in light blue. During the postseason, the Brewers are 4-0 in cream and 3-1 in navy.
Tampa Bay was 36-19 in home white, 32-33 in road navy, 8-2 in road Columbia blue, 12-3 in Devil Rays throwback jerseys, 6-4 in City Connect and 3-3 in road gray. In the playoffs, the Rays are 2-1 in home white, 2-0 in Devil Rays throwbacks and 3-1 in road gray.
Mirror mirror
Milwaukee was 32 for 128 (.250) and had a .347 on-base percentage in its NLCS sweep of the Dodgers, the exact same numbers Los Angeles batters had in their NLCS sweep of the Brewers last year.
